newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report. [CORRECTED 18:33 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report. [CORRECTED 18:33 GMT]

text.p: Spanish government long-term bonds ended lower but off lows on Monday amid dull trade, while the yield curve steepened thanks to a stronger peseta.
"What we have is mainly a very weak Deutsche mark. But this is supporting the short end of the yield curve," a dealer said.
He added that today's correction came amid very light trade "and that it was very healthy".
Despite the peseta's strength, dealers expect no cut in Tuesday's Bank of Spain official repo. The central bank is seen holding the key money market rate at 5.25 percent.
"The latest inflation figure was not bad. But surely it was nothing that could push the Bank of Spain to cut its rate," a dealer said.
June CPI rose 1.6 percent year on year versus May's 1.5 pct.

Dealers said Tuesday's market focus would be on the U.S. June CPI figure, due on Wednesday (corrects to make clear figure due Wednesday), which "given the good industrial production price data are expected to be good", a dealer said. Consensus expectations are for U.S. CPI to climb 0.2 percent in June to 2.4 percent in the year.
The Spanish 10-year spread over Bunds was unchanged from morning trading at around 63 basis points.
